From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Latency measurement & SLO playbook — TradeWinds follow-up

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and immediate asks so we can turn this into a short SLO playbook for your procurement/security teams. I pasted the notes and the two example payload traces as attachments.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: clinical documentation assistant (short prompts, streaming partial answers to UI) + occasional batch summarization jobs.
- Expected steady QPS: 10–20 rps during business hours; burst up to ~120 rps for 5–10 minute windows tied to shift changes.
- Concurrent long-lived streaming sessions: ~60 active at peak (each streaming partial tokens every 300–800ms).
- Target latency thresholds you mentioned on the call: customer-perceived streaming responsiveness around 300–500ms for first token, and 95th tail for non-streaming calls ~150–200ms (you said you would confirm exact numbers).

Immediate asks from us
1) Confirm the latency targets you want codified (95th/99th and streaming first-token/stream tail).
2) Confirm whether you want latency measured server-side at Redwood egress (our default) or end-to-end from the client (we can support both but wording matters).
3) Share any example traces or a short week-of-traffic sample if possible (attached sample_payloads_traffic_profile.jsonl is our schema).

Next steps (proposed schedule)
- Fri 2026-11-23 EOD: Redwood to send draft SLO/SLA language + measurement method + exclusion list (we will include remedies table).
- Week of 2026-11-29: joint review with TradeWinds security/procurement to finalize wording.

Attachments: meeting-notes-20261122.pdf, sample_payloads_traffic_profile.jsonl

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if you prefer to run through the draft live.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Latency measurement & SLO playbook — TradeWinds follow-up

Monica —

Thanks for the concise recap and for the attachments, very helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Confirmed targets (internal):
   - Non-streaming request 95th ≤ 150 ms; 99th ≤ 300 ms.
   - Streaming: first-token ≤ 300 ms; steady streaming increment delivery (we care less about every chunk but want to avoid visible pauses > 800 ms).

2) Measurement preference: for procurement we prefer "server-side observed" latency (Redwood egress) as the canonical measurement for SLA disputes, but we also want an option to request end-to-end samples if we suspect client-side network issues.

3) Traffic sample: I attached a small set of traces we anonymized; hope that helps (I'll send a secure link to the larger trace set to your SRE alias if needed).

4) Timeline: Procurement wants the formal SLO/SLA language and a one-page measurement note by the end of next week (2026-11-30) to include in their internal review. Security will need the measurement method + evidence of auditability.

Couple of questions for Redwood:
- How do you treat scheduled maintenance windows for SLO calculation? Is there a canon exclusion window or do you prorate?
- For streaming sessions where the client cancels mid-stream, does that count as a failed sample or is it excluded?

Appreciate you leading here.

—Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Integrations | TradeWinds Health
alex.mercer@tradewindshealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0122

Alex / Monica —

Thanks for the details, Alex. A couple of quick clarifications and a proposed draft snippet for the SLA measurement section below — putting this in short form so procurement/security can paste directly into their doc. I attached a first-pass Word doc (draft-slo-v1.docx) with the full table of remedies.

Proposed measurement & exclusions (draft):
- Measurement point: server-side egress latency measured at Redwood's inference gateway, computed per-request as time from request receipt to final token emission (non-streaming) and time to first token for streaming.
- Distribution windows: compute 95th and 99th percentiles on a daily rolling window; monthly reporting will provide aggregated percentiles and incident history.
- Exclusions:
  1) Scheduled maintenance windows > 15 minutes announced 72 hours in advance.
  2) Customer-originated network interruptions (determined by traceroute/edge logs or by mutual agreement).
  3) Requests where client request size > 128k characters (we'll flag these as outliers and exclude from percentile computation).
  4) Cancelled client streaming sessions where no server-side tokens were emitted. Partially completed streams (server emitted >=1 token) are measured as normal.
- Remedies: service credits tied to monthly P95/P99 breach thresholds; see attached table.

Notes:
- We default to server-side measurement for contractual clarity but can include an "end-to-end samples" clause allowing TradeWinds to request E2E capture for disputed incidents (we would coordinate dates and share sanitized packet logs).
- Reporting cadence: monthly SLA report (automated) + ad-hoc incident reports within 24 hours of a detected breach.

If that looks reasonable I can push the draft into the shared HubSpot doc and Marissa can add the legal-friendly language for the MSA amendment.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Alex / team —

Thanks for the quick replies and for the trace extracts. Based on Ben's draft and your confirmation, below is a clean SLO/SLA paragraph and the remedies summary we propose for inclusion in the MSA amendment. Please review and flag any items that need legal/security-specific phrasing. If this looks fine, I'll circulate a DocuSign packet for the amendment + measurement note.

Suggested SLA language (contract-ready)
1) Measurement: Redwood Inference shall measure request latency at Redwood's inference gateway (server-side egress). For non-streaming requests, latency is measured as time from request receipt to final token emission. For streaming requests, the primary SLO is time-to-first-token; subsequent token delivery consistency is handled via an availability check that flags gaps > 800 ms. 95th and 99th percentile latencies will be computed on a rolling 24-hour window and reported monthly.

2) Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance (announced ≥72 hours in advance and longer than 15 minutes); catastrophic region-wide failures; customer-originated network outages (validated through mutual logs); requests exceeding 128k character payloads; streaming sessions cancelled prior to any server-side token emission.

3) Reporting cadence & auditability: Redwood will provide an automated monthly SLA report (percentiles, sample traces for any breaches, incident timeline). TradeWinds may request end-to-end samples for specific incidents; such requests will be responded to within 5 business days and may require redacted logs.

4) Remedies: Monthly service credits as follows: if monthly P95 > 150 ms, 5% service credit; if monthly P99 > 300 ms, 10% service credit; catastrophic availability (monthly availability < 99.0%) triggers 20% credit and escalation. Credits apply to hosting/inference fees for the affected month only.

Next steps
- I will upload the draft to the HubSpot deal record and create a one-page measurement note (link below).
- If acceptable, I'll start DocuSign for the MSA amendment and the measurement note by EOD 2026-11-24.
- Suggest a 30-minute sync on 2026-11-29 to review the monitoring dashboard and acceptance tests.
